summary: Learning tile: a dedicated Atlas Shell application entry that surfaces TaskTracker training_unit tasks with progress, markdown-defined potential subtasks, and child-task activation — implemented entirely as a frontend-only tile backed by TaskTracker API extensions.

classification.why_application: Owns the Learning domain UI, defines learning-specific sort rules, parses the markdown potential-subtask contract, and interprets training_unit task semantics — none of which belong in a generic platform service. The TaskTracker schema extensions are domain-carrying additions to an existing application.
non_goals: No new backend service — all persistence is owned by TaskTracker
No LearningGoal, LearningMean, or LearningSession objects
No server-side markdown storage — the ## Potential Subtasks section lives inside task.description
classification.not_platform: All behavior is specific to the Learning domain concept. The markdown parsing and training_unit semantics have no generic reuse value across Atlas.

consumes: TaskTracker GET /api/tasks/training-units — returns Dataset of training_unit tasks with derived fields: last_child_completed_at, completed_child_count, total_child_count, labels embedded; sorted DONE first by last_child_completed_at DESC then OPEN by priority DESC
TaskTracker POST /api/tasks — create task; accepts task_type, parent_task_id, actual_duration_minutes, completed_at in addition to existing fields
TaskTracker PATCH /api/tasks/{task_id} — partial update; accepts task_type, actual_duration_minutes, completed_at; sets completed_at = now() server-side when status transitions to done
TaskTracker GET /api/tasks — excludes task_type = training_unit by default; returns training_session tasks as normal tasks

TaskTracker GET /api/tasks?task_type=training_session&parent_task_id=<uuid> — fetches child training_session tasks for a given parent training_unit; parameters: task_type=training_session (required, fixed), parent_task_id (uuid, required); ordering: created_at ASC; empty-result behavior: return empty rows array; time basis: server
TaskTracker GET /api/tasks/{task_id}/labels — labels on one task (existing)
TaskTracker PUT /api/tasks/{task_id}/labels — replace all labels on a task (existing)
provides: Learning tile registered in Atlas Shell navigation under appId=learning, basePath=/learning
Training unit list view: displays each training_unit task with title, labels, priority, progress bar, last activity date, potential subtasks (parsed from description), and active child tasks
Subtask activation: promotes a markdown unchecked line into a training_session task linked to the parent, updates description markdown in-place
Child task duration update: user can update actual_duration_minutes on training_session tasks from the Learning tile
invariants: The Learning tile only displays task_type = training_unit tasks
The main TaskTracker task list excludes task_type = training_unit tasks
All API calls from the Learning frontend route through the TaskTracker backend — no direct calls to LabelEngine
A potential subtask line - [ ] <title> is only promoted once; after promotion it becomes - [x] <title> → task: <uuid> in the description
Activated subtask tasks are created with task_type = training_session, parent_task_id = parent unit id, status = open
completed_at is set server-side by TaskTracker when status transitions to done — the frontend does not supply it
All read endpoints return Dataset per R-CON-BP-04

Label inheritance on activation: the child task receives the same labels as the parent training_unit at creation time; labels are applied via PUT /api/tasks/{id}/labels immediately after task creation
failure_modes: TASKTRACKER_UNAVAILABLE — TaskTracker backend unreachable; Learning tile shows ErrorCard; no silent degradation on the units list
TRAINING_UNITS_EMPTY — no training_unit tasks exist; tile shows an empty-state message
SUBTASK_ACTIVATION_FAILED — POST /api/tasks fails; error shown inline; description not updated
DESCRIPTION_UPDATE_FAILED — PATCH /api/tasks/{id} fails after task creation; task exists but description still shows unchecked; user must retry or manually update
LABEL_INHERIT_FAILED — PUT /api/tasks/{id}/labels fails after creation; task created without inherited labels; error surfaced inline

consumes: TaskTracker TrainingUnitRow: {id, title, description, status, priority, labels: [{id, name}], last_child_completed_at: str|null (ISO datetime), completed_child_count: int, total_child_count: int, actual_duration_minutes: int|null, completed_at: str|null} — emitted by GET /api/tasks/training-units
TaskTracker HTTP API at TASKTRACKER_URL (env var resolved via Nginx proxy at /tasks/) — all endpoints listed in contracts.consumes
AppRegistry.register() from @atlas/shell — side-effect import from shellConfig.ts
provides: Atlas Shell navigation entry: appId=learning, label=Learning, basePath=/learning
Route /learning — LearningPage showing training unit list
Route /learning/:unitId — UnitDetailPage (unit detail, potential subtasks, child tasks)

exposed_surfaces.name: shellConfig.ts side-effect import
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Registers the Learning tile in the Atlas Shell navigation via AppRegistry.register()

exposed_surfaces.name: /learning
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Lists all training_unit tasks with progress and last activity; sorted DONE first, then OPEN by priority

exposed_surfaces.name: /learning/new
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Form to create a new training_unit task with title, description (including ## Potential Subtasks), priority, and labels

exposed_surfaces.name: /learning/:unitId
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Detail view for a training_unit: shows parsed potential subtasks with activation buttons, active child tasks with duration editing

internal_flow.name: shell_registration
internal_flow.description: shellConfig.ts is imported as a side-effect by Atlas Shell main.tsx. It calls AppRegistry.register() with appId=learning, basePath=/learning, component=React.lazy(ShellEntry), and nav items.
outputs: Learning tile visible in Atlas Shell navigation

internal_flow.name: learning_list_load
internal_flow.description: On /learning mount, LearningPage fetches GET /tasks/training-units. Response is a Dataset with TrainingUnitRow rows. Frontend derives progress = completed_child_count / total_child_count (0 if total_child_count = 0). Rows are already sorted server-side.
outputs: Rendered list of training unit cards with title, labels, priority chip, progress bar (completed/total), last activity date (last_child_completed_at), status badge

internal_flow.name: potential_subtask_parsing
internal_flow.description: Frontend parses task.description to extract the ## Potential Subtasks section. Lines matching '- [ ] <title>' are unchecked (activatable). Lines matching '- [x] <title> → task: <uuid>' are checked (already activated). Parsing is client-side, purely string-based. No regex library required — simple line-by-line scan.
outputs: unchecked_lines: {lineText: string}[], activated_lines: {lineText: string, taskId: string}[]

internal_flow.name: subtask_activation
internal_flow.description: User clicks 'Create task' on an unchecked potential subtask line. Frontend: (1) POST /tasks with {title: lineText, task_type: training_session, parent_task_id: unit.id, status: open, priority: inherit from parent}. (2) If parent has labels, PUT /tasks/{newId}/labels with parent label names. (3) PATCH /tasks/{unit.id} to update description: replace '- [ ] <title>' with '- [x] <title> → task: <uuid>'. Errors at each step are surfaced inline; step 3 failure leaves the task created but description unupdated.
outputs: new training_session task created and linked
UI re-renders activated line as checked

internal_flow.name: child_task_duration_update
internal_flow.description: From UnitDetailPage, user edits actual_duration_minutes on a visible child training_session task. Frontend calls PATCH /tasks/{childId} with {actual_duration_minutes: value}. On success, updates local state.
outputs: updated task row returned as Dataset (single row)

internal_flow.name: training_unit_creation
internal_flow.description: CreateTrainingUnitPage submits POST /tasks with {title, description (including ## Potential Subtasks section if provided), task_type: training_unit, status: open, priority}. After creation, PUT /tasks/{id}/labels if labels were specified. Redirects to /learning on success.

internal_required.role: Sole data source; provides all task persistence, training_unit endpoint, label management proxy. PersonalDevelopment is a pure consumer of TaskTracker APIs.
Shell registration via AppRegistry.register(); provides @atlas/shell import alias, shared UI components (ErrorCard, Skeleton), and apiFetch client
Dataset and ApiError types — imported from canonical path for TypeScript type safety

PersonalDevelopment introducing a new backend service
PersonalDevelopment owning any Postgres tables — all persistence owned by TaskTracker
Using LinkingEngine for parent-child relationships — controlled deviation: parent_task_id column on tasktracker.tasks is used instead
Setting completed_at from the frontend — TaskTracker backend sets it server-side on status=done transition

persistence.ownership: none — all persistence owned by TaskTracker
persistence.notes: PersonalDevelopment does not own a schema. The 10_schema.sql artifact contains ALTER TABLE migrations against tasktracker.tasks (owned by TaskTracker). These columns are added to TaskTracker's existing table to support the Learning domain. The migration is applied via TaskTracker's schema initialization path or as a separate migration script.

risks.risk: GET /api/tasks training_unit exclusion breaks existing TaskTracker tests or client behavior
risks.impact: Existing active-view and pending-board tests may fail if fixtures contain training_unit tasks; implementer must audit existing fixtures and ensure the exclusion is additive-only for new fixture rows

risks.risk: Description PATCH race condition on subtask activation
risks.impact: If two subtasks are activated near-simultaneously, the second PATCH may overwrite the first activation marker in the description. Mitigated by single-user context — documented as known limitation

risks.risk: completed_at server-side assignment relies on PATCH detecting status transition to done
risks.impact: If PATCH is called with status=done but completed_at already set, server must not overwrite it. Implementer must check: only set completed_at = now() if status transitions TO done AND completed_at IS NULL in the existing row

open_questions.question: Should GET /api/tasks/training-units support pagination or return all units in one page? Training units are expected to be few (<100), so a single-page response may be sufficient.

Should child tasks (training_session) be fetched in the UnitDetailPage via a dedicated endpoint or via GET /api/tasks?parent_task_id=<uuid>? The latter requires adding a parent_task_id query param to GET /api/tasks.
